findings.location: src/http/process-projection.ts:isInstanceParticipantBatch fallback-slug lookup (~L1423); src/__tests__/processes-read-visibility.test.ts (no test ever supplies a distinct fallbackSlug)
findings.issue: T-0765 closes the fake-green gap (T-0715 class) for the DETAIL point-lookup and the batch PRIMARY lookup (mutations A/B both reproduce RED as claimed), but the batch FALLBACK-slug lookup remains invisible to this fast unit test file if its ACTOR_ACTIVE_SQL predicate were ever removed — not because the fake-pool's routing is wrong (the same `carriesActiveGate` check would apply if exercised) but because NO test in the file ever passes a fallbackSlug argument at all, so the branch containing that lookup is never entered. The builder's own pr-handoff.json follow_ups claims the fixed fake-pool 'covers it by construction' — judge's direct mutation (probe C above) shows this specific committed suite stays 28/28 GREEN, i.e. the claim is not accurate for the CURRENT test inputs.
findings.suggestion: Non-blocking: (1) fallbackSlug is undefined at both current production call sites, so this is currently dead code, matching the task's own stated resolution criterion; (2) an independent, pre-existing static gate (ci/checks/actor-authority-deactivation-gate.sh, FF-0662-1) DOES catch removal of this predicate regardless of unit-test reachability (judge reproduced the FAIL directly on the mutated tree). Recommend a follow-up task to either (a) add an explicit unit case that calls the batch fn with a distinct, deactivated fallbackSlug through the fixed fake-pool to get fast-tier RED coverage before fallbackSlug is ever wired to a real caller, or (b) narrow the pr-handoff.json/module-comment claim to state the fallback path's fast-tier guard is currently FF-0662-1 (static), not the fake-pool simulation, so future readers don't over-trust unit coverage there.
